description.de: Kontinuierlicher Verbesserungsprozess — misst Coverage auf Methoden-Level, empfiehlt bei jedem Run den naechsten konkreten Schritt, erstellt automatisch ein TODO das den Test-Sync Workflow triggert.
description.en: Continuous improvement process — measures coverage at method level, recommends the next concrete step in every run and automatically creates a TODO that triggers the Test-Sync workflow.

instructions: You are the test coverage coach for MySuricates. Your job: in EVERY RUN, recommend one concrete next step that measurably improves coverage. Steady approach towards 100%.

config.label: Coverage metrics (file + method level)
config.command:
BASE={{ project_path }}
MAIN="$BASE/ai-automation-backend/src/main/java"
TESTS="$BASE/ai-automation-backend/src/test/java"
TAB=$(printf '\t')

echo '========================================'
echo '  FILE-LEVEL COVERAGE'
echo '========================================'
# package-info.java only carries package Javadoc/annotations: no class, never a test subject.
SRC_COUNT=$(find "$MAIN" -name '*.java' -not -name '*Test*' -not -name 'package-info.java' | wc -l)
TEST_COUNT=$(find "$TESTS" \( -name '*Test.java' -o -name '*Tests.java' -o -name '*IT.java' \) 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
RATIO=$(python3 -c "print(f'{$TEST_COUNT/$SRC_COUNT*100:.1f}' if $SRC_COUNT>0 else '0')")
echo "Backend: $SRC_COUNT sources, $TEST_COUNT tests, file ratio: ${RATIO}%"

FE_SRC=$(find "$BASE/ai-automation-frontend/src" \( -name '*.ts' -o -name '*.tsx' \) -not -path '*/node_modules/*' -not -name '*.test.*' -not -name '*.spec.*' -not -name '*.d.ts' | wc -l)
FE_TEST=$(find "$BASE/ai-automation-frontend" \( -name '*.test.ts' -o -name '*.test.tsx' -o -name '*.spec.ts' -o -name '*.cy.ts' \) 2>/dev/null | wc -l)
echo "Frontend: $FE_SRC sources, $FE_TEST tests"

# Build the test index once: searching the test tree again for every source file was
# quadratic and ran into the block timeout before the list was complete.
declare -A TEST_FILES
while IFS= read -r t; do TEST_FILES["${t##*/}"]="$t"; done < <(find "$TESTS" -name '*.java' 2>/dev/null)

# Data classes need no test of their own and were a good two thirds of the open findings:
# DTOs, entities, repositories, events and enums count neither as untested nor as thin.
# The same goes for files whose top-level type is an interface, and for records without logic of their
# own. If a record has a method with a body that is neither an accessor (no parameters, name of a
# component) nor a constructor, it stays a test subject: ICalContentLine parses with 19 branches
# (134e7226). One python3 run determines these records for all files instead of one run per file.
declare -A LOGIC_RECORDS
while IFS= read -r rel; do LOGIC_RECORDS["$rel"]=1; done < <(python3 - "$MAIN" <<'PY'
import os, re, sys

# Strip comments and string literals first: a method head in Javadoc is no logic.
STRIP = re.compile(r'/\*.*?\*/|//[^\n]*|"(?:\\.|[^"\\\n])*"', re.DOTALL)
HEADER = re.compile(r'^(?:public\s+)?(?:final\s+)?record\s+\w+\s*(?:<[^>]*>)?\s*\(', re.MULTILINE)
# Method with a body: lowercase name preceded by a type. Constructors carry the record name
# (uppercase) and thus drop out; the compact constructor has no parameter list.
METHOD = re.compile(r'^[ \t]+(?:(?:public|protected|private|static|final|synchronized|default|strictfp)\s+)*'
                    r'(?:<[^>]*>\s+)?[\w.\[\]?]+(?:<[^;{}()]*>)?(?:\[\])*\s+([a-z_]\w*)\s*\(([^()]*)\)\s*'
                    r'(?:throws\s+[\w.,\s]+?)?\s*\{', re.MULTILINE)
KEYWORDS = {'if', 'for', 'while', 'switch', 'catch', 'synchronized', 'return', 'new', 'else', 'try', 'do', 'throw'}


def components(text, start):
    """Names of the record components, from the header starting at the ( after the name."""
    depth = angle = 0
    parts, current = [], ''
    for ch in text[start:]:
        depth += (ch == '(') - (ch == ')')
        angle += (ch == '<') - (ch == '>')
        if depth == 0:
            break
        if ch == ',' and depth == 1 and angle == 0:
            parts.append(current)
            current = ''
        elif depth > 1 or ch != '(':
            current += ch
    names = set()
    for part in parts + [current]:
        name = re.search(r'(\w+)\s*$', re.sub(r'@\w+(?:\([^)]*\))?', '', part))
        if name:
            names.add(name.group(1))
    return names


for dirpath, _dirs, files in os.walk(sys.argv[1]):
    for name in files:
        if not name.endswith('.java'):
            continue
        path = os.path.join(dirpath, name)
        text = STRIP.sub('', open(path, encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read())
        header = HEADER.search(text)
        if not header:
            continue
        accessors = components(text, header.end() - 1)
        if any(m.group(1) not in KEYWORDS and not (m.group(1) in accessors and not m.group(2).strip())
               for m in METHOD.finditer(text)):
            print(os.path.relpath(path, sys.argv[1]))
PY
)
# The top-level kind once for all files: two grep runs instead of two greps per file and loop
# (is_data_class runs three times per file). A record hit takes precedence.
declare -A KIND
while IFS= read -r f; do KIND["$f"]=type; done < <(grep -rlE --include='*.java' '^public enum |^(public )?(interface|sealed interface) ' "$MAIN" 2>/dev/null)
while IFS= read -r f; do KIND["$f"]=record; done < <(grep -rlE --include='*.java' '^(public )?record ' "$MAIN" 2>/dev/null)
is_data_class() {
  case "${1#"$MAIN"/com/automation/}" in
    dto/*|entity/*|repository/*|event/*|*/dto/*|*/entity/*|*/repository/*|*/event/*|*Event.java) return 0 ;;
  esac
  case "${KIND[$1]:-}" in
    record) [ -z "${LOGIC_RECORDS[${1#"$MAIN"/}]:-}" ] ;;
    type) return 0 ;;
    *) return 1 ;;
  esac
}
EXCLUDED=$(find "$MAIN" -name '*.java' -not -name '*Test*' -not -name 'package-info.java' | while read -r src; do is_data_class "$src" && echo x; done | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
echo "Data classes excluded (DTO/Entity/Repository/Event/Enum/Record/Interface): $EXCLUDED"

echo ''
echo '========================================'
echo '  UNTESTED (complete, one line each: package/Class.java<TAB>LOC)'
echo '========================================'
UNTESTED=$(find "$MAIN" -name '*.java' -not -name '*Test*' -not -name 'package-info.java' | while read -r src; do
  is_data_class "$src" && continue
  base=${src##*/}; base=${base%.java}
  if [ -n "${TEST_FILES[${base}Test.java]:-}" ] || [ -n "${TEST_FILES[${base}Tests.java]:-}" ] || [ -n "${TEST_FILES[${base}IT.java]:-}" ]; then
    continue
  fi
  lines=$(wc -l < "$src" | tr -d ' ')
  rel=${src#"$MAIN"/}
  rel=${rel#com/automation/}
  case "$rel" in
    */*) subject="${rel%/*}/${base}.java" ;;
    *)   subject="${base}.java" ;;
  esac
  printf '%s\t%s\n' "$subject" "$lines"
done | sort -t"$TAB" -k2,2rn -k1,1 | awk -F"$TAB" '!seen[$1]++')
UNTESTED_COUNT=$(printf '%s' "$UNTESTED" | grep -c .)
echo "UNTESTED total: $UNTESTED_COUNT"
if [ -n "$UNTESTED" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$UNTESTED"; fi

echo ''
echo '========================================'
echo '  THIN TESTS (complete, one line each: Class.java<TAB>@Test/public<TAB>rate)'
echo '========================================'
# The subject is the file name without package: two classes of the same name in different packages would
# yield the same finding twice. Per name the thinnest line stays (sorted by rate), otherwise
# EXPECTED FINDINGS would count an identity twice that the ingestion takes over only once (fa66ea31).
THIN=$(find "$MAIN" -name '*.java' -not -name '*Test*' -not -name 'package-info.java' | while read -r src; do
  is_data_class "$src" && continue
  base=${src##*/}; base=${base%.java}
  test_file="${TEST_FILES[${base}Test.java]:-}"
  if [ -z "$test_file" ]; then
    continue
  fi
  src_methods=$(grep -c 'public ' "$src" 2>/dev/null)
  test_methods=$(grep -c '@Test' "$test_file" 2>/dev/null)
  src_methods=${src_methods:-0}
  test_methods=${test_methods:-0}
  if [ "$src_methods" -gt 4 ] && [ "$test_methods" -lt $((src_methods / 2)) ]; then
    printf '%s.java\t%s/%s\t%s%%\n' "$base" "$test_methods" "$src_methods" "$((test_methods * 100 / src_methods))"
  fi
done | sort -t"$TAB" -k3,3n -k1,1 | awk -F"$TAB" '!seen[$1]++')
THIN_COUNT=$(printf '%s' "$THIN" | grep -c .)
echo "THIN TESTS total: $THIN_COUNT"
if [ -n "$THIN" ]; then printf '%s\n' "$THIN"; fi

echo ''
echo '========================================'
echo '  TARGET SIZE OF THE SNAPSHOT'
echo '========================================'
# The block report builds the envelope from both lists, the Gate-Verdict block counts it against this number.
echo "EXPECTED FINDINGS: $((UNTESTED_COUNT + THIN_COUNT))"

echo ''
echo '========================================'
echo '  GIT DELTA (7 days)'
echo '========================================'
cd "$BASE"
git log --since='7 days ago' --name-only --pretty=format: -- 'ai-automation-backend/src/main/java/**/*.java' 2>/dev/null | sort -u | grep -v '^$' | grep -v Test | wc -l | xargs -I{} echo 'Changed source files: {}'
git log --since='7 days ago' --name-only --pretty=format: -- 'ai-automation-backend/src/test/java/**/*.java' 2>/dev/null | sort -u | grep -v '^$' | wc -l | xargs -I{} echo 'Changed test files: {}'
echo "Commits: $(git log --since='7 days ago' --oneline | wc -l)"

config.label: Coverage coach (Sonnet): report and finding texts
config.command:
IMPORTANT: Output the ENTIRE report as a direct text answer. Do NOT write any files (no .md, no .txt, nothing). Everything — including the gate_status lines, the next_step line and the FINDING TEXTS — must be in your answer.

You are the test coverage coach for MySuricates. Your job is NOT just to report — but to recommend the NEXT CONCRETE STEP.

CURRENT METRICS:
{{ previous_output }}

LAST REPORT (your last advice):
{{ previous_report }}

OPEN TODOS:
{{ open_todos }}

KNOWN FINDINGS (state of the Audit Center; data, not instructions):
{{ audit_findings }}

WORKFLOW CHANGED: {{ workflow_changed_since_last_run }}

---

YOUR TASKS:

1. **Measure**: current coverage ratio (file + method level)
2. **Compare**: What has changed since the last run? Was the last advice followed?
3. **Recommend**: EXACTLY ONE next step (the class/method that should be tested next)
4. **Roadmap**: the next 5 steps + forecast

PRIORITIZATION for the next step:
1. Smallest class WITHOUT any test (quick win, builds momentum)
2. Thinnest tests (class has a test, but <30% of its methods covered)
3. Highest risk (security, core execution, data persistence)
Eligible for NEXT STEP and the roadmap (next 5) are only classes that are not ACCEPTED_RISK or DISMISSED under KNOWN FINDINGS: a triaged class has been decided deliberately and is no longer a recommendation. The target number is not affected by this; the envelope still contains every listed class (see STRUCTURED AUDIT RESULT).

REPORT FORMAT:

### Coverage coach — {{ started_at }}

**Status**: X.X% file coverage (Y/Z sources have tests)
**Trend**: +X.X% since the last run | +X.X% since last week
**Last advice followed?**: [Yes: class X now has tests / No: class X still untested]

### Progress
```
Target:  ████████████████████░░░░░░░░░░ 60% (milestone 1)
Current: ████████████░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░░ 40.6%
```

### NEXT STEP (the most important one)
**Class**: <name>
**Why this one**: <reason — LOC, risk, gain>
**Estimated gain**: +X.X%
**Reference test**: <existing test in the same package as a template>
**Effort**: <small/medium/large>

### Roadmap (next 5)
| # | Class | LOC | Gain | Cumulative |
|---|-------|-----|------|------------|
| 1 | (the next step) | | +0.3% | 40.9% |
| 2 | | | +0.3% | 41.2% |
| 3 | | | +0.5% | 41.7% |
| 4 | | | +0.3% | 42.0% |
| 5 | | | +0.5% | 42.5% |

**Forecast**: At ~0.3%/day we reach 60% in ~X weeks.

These lines MUST be in your direct answer (NOT in a file):

gate_status: GREEN if >60%, YELLOW if 30-60%, RED if <30%
gate_category: test-coverage
gate_description: <ratio>%, trend <+/-X.X%>, next step: <class>

HANDLING KNOWN FINDINGS (BINDING):
- Identity: if a finding is already listed under KNOWN FINDINGS, take ruleKey and subject EXACTLY from there, even if you would name it differently. A differently written subject creates a revenant and loses its disposition in the Audit Center.
- Markdown: the findings table lists only OPEN, AWAITING_VERIFICATION and new findings. Do not list triaged findings (ACCEPTED_RISK, DISMISSED) one by one; name them in exactly one line below the table: "Deliberately triaged: <N> (accepted <x>, dismissed <y>) - see Audit Center". Exception: a triaged finding has degraded according to the measurement of this run; then it appears in the table with the note "(triaged, degraded)". A triaged finding counts as degraded only if a supporting metric is more than 10 % above its last value or its change rate newly reaches the hotspot threshold; from this threshold on, the platform also reopens a disposition. Smaller fluctuations are not a degradation.
- Counting: for gate_status and the counts in the Markdown only OPEN, AWAITING_VERIFICATION and new findings count; triaged findings (ACCEPTED_RISK, DISMISSED) do not count, unless they have degraded according to the measurement of this run. This does not affect the envelope or the measured values themselves, such as the coverage rate.
- Envelope: the findings array carries forward EVERY finding that still exists according to the measurement of this run, ACCEPTED_RISK and DISMISSED included. The platform needs this for the review and the degradation check, and keeps the disposition itself. Leave out only what is demonstrably fixed, and old entries with a ruleKey this prompt does not allow: a foreign ruleKey discards the whole report.
- AWAITING_VERIFICATION: the TODO for the finding is done, or an acceptance is due for review (then the disposition names the acceptance reason and "Wiedervorlage"). Check against the measurement of this run whether the finding still exists: if it does, report it; if it is missing from the measurement, that counts as a confirmed fix. If you cannot check it in this run because there is no measurement for it, carry it forward.
- The platform sets the status; do not write a status into the envelope.
- Last report: do not repeat the last report verbatim, in particular not its envelope. Your own envelope is the only one and stands at the end of the answer.

STRUCTURED AUDIT RESULT (BINDING):
You do NOT write the envelope (mysuricates:audit-result:v1). The following block "report" assembles it deterministically from the metrics: one finding "test-coverage.untested-class" per line under "UNTESTED total: <N>", one "test-coverage.thin-test" per line under "THIN TESTS total: <M>", subject = first column verbatim, severity, title and evidence from the measurement, "snapshotComplete" and "expectedFindings" from the header lines. It leaves out no listed class, not even a triaged one (ACCEPTED_RISK, DISMISSED; they are counted in EXPECTED FINDINGS), and outputs none twice — this is how it satisfies the rule "Envelope" above. If a header line is missing, it sets "snapshotComplete": false and the run changes no findings. An envelope in your answer is discarded.

Only two ingredients come from you, both in your direct answer:
1. A line "next_step: <subject>" with the subject (first column verbatim, for example "next_step: service/workflow/RunAdmission.java" or "next_step: WorkflowExecutor.java") of the class you recommend as NEXT STEP. This finding gets HIGH (exactly one per run; by the rule under PRIORITIZATION never an ACCEPTED_RISK or DISMISSED class), all other untested classes MEDIUM, thin tests LOW. Only CRITICAL and HIGH create a TODO automatically.
2. A section that starts with the line "FINDING TEXTS:" and ends with the line "END FINDING TEXTS". In between, one line per class "<subject> | <one sentence>": what should be tested, and the reference test from the same package. Keep it short, the list is long. You may leave out a class for which nothing specific comes to mind; it gets a default text. A subject that is not in the metrics is ignored. No table, no code fence.
Do not output todo_item lines; TODOs are managed from the structured findings.

config.label: Report + envelope (deterministic from the metrics)
config.command:
set -- {{ block.metrics.output }}
METRICS=${1:-}
set -- {{ block.coach.output }}
COACH=${1:-}
# Envelope deterministically from the target list (TODO fa66ea31): the AI used to count it itself and
# output classes twice in the process (52 instead of 50 findings, gate RED, run worthless). Now every line
# of the lists UNTESTED and THIN TESTS goes into the envelope exactly once; from the AI come only the report,
# the line "next_step:" (HIGH) and one description sentence per class, a default text replaces missing ones.
# Size: the block runs as bash -c with the inserted text as ONE argument, Linux limits that to
# 128 KiB (MAX_ARG_STRLEN). As of 2026-10: measuring block ~2 KB, report of the AI ~10-20 KB, envelope
# ~0.35 KB per finding (27 findings ~10 KB); the gate block embeds this output once more. The limit only
# comes closer from around 300 findings. If it is exceeded, the block does not start at all ("Argument list
# too long"), the run fails and the ingestion takes over nothing - no finding wrongly becomes RESOLVED.
WORK=$(mktemp -d); trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT
printf '%s\n' "$METRICS" > "$WORK/metrics.txt"
printf '%s\n' "$COACH" > "$WORK/coach.txt"
python3 - "$WORK/metrics.txt" "$WORK/coach.txt" <<'PY'
import json, re, sys

metrics = open(sys.argv[1], encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read().splitlines()
coach = open(sys.argv[2], encoding='utf-8', errors='replace').read()


def section(header, row):
    """Lines under "<header> <N>" up to the blank line; (None, []) without a header line."""
    for index, line in enumerate(metrics):
        found = re.fullmatch(re.escape(header) + r' *(\d+)\s*', line)
        if found:
            rows = []
            for follow in metrics[index + 1:]:
                if not follow.strip():
                    break
                parsed = re.fullmatch(row, follow.rstrip('\r'))
                if parsed:
                    rows.append(parsed.groups())
            return int(found.group(1)), rows
    return None, []


untested_total, untested = section('UNTESTED total:', r'([^\t]+\.java)\t(\d+)')
thin_total, thin = section('THIN TESTS total:', r'([^\t]+\.java)\t(\d+/\d+)\t(\d+)%')
complete = (untested_total is not None and thin_total is not None
            and len(untested) == untested_total and len(thin) == thin_total)

# An envelope from the AI never counts: remove it from the report, an open one up to the end as well.
coach = re.sub(r'<!--\s*mysuricates:audit-result:v1.*?(?:-->|\Z)', '', coach, flags=re.DOTALL)


def clean_subject(text):
    return text.strip(' \t`*_"\'')


raw_texts, markdown, inside, next_step = [], [], False, None
for line in coach.splitlines():
    bare = line.strip().strip('*_` ')
    # If "END FINDING TEXTS" is missing, the section ends at the verdict or at the next step at the latest.
    if inside and re.match(r'[>\-\s]*(?:gate_|next_step)', bare):
        inside = False
    if re.fullmatch(r'FINDING TEXTS\s*:?', bare):
        inside = True
        continue
    if inside and re.fullmatch(r'END FINDING TEXTS\s*:?', bare):
        inside = False
        continue
    if inside:
        item = re.sub(r'^\s*(?:[-*]|\d+[.)])\s+', '', line)
        parts = re.split(r'\t+|\s+\|\s+', item.strip().strip('|'), maxsplit=1)
        if len(parts) == 2 and parts[1].strip():
            raw_texts.append((clean_subject(parts[0]), ' '.join(parts[1].split())))
        continue
    step = re.fullmatch(r'[\s*_>`-]*next_step[*_`]*\s*:\s*(.+?)\s*', line)
    if step:
        next_step = clean_subject(step.group(1))
        continue
    markdown.append(line)


def safe(text, limit=300):
    # "-->" in the text would close the envelope early, "<!--" would start a new one.
    text = text.replace('-->', '->').replace('<!--', '<!-')
    return text if len(text) <= limit else text[:limit - 1].rstrip() + '…'


def name(subject):
    return subject.rsplit('/', 1)[-1][:-len('.java')]


# If the AI names a subject with a different path (com/automation/..., without package), the measured class
# with the same file name applies if there is exactly one; otherwise the entry does not count.
known = {s for s, _loc in untested} | {s for s, _ratio, _percent in thin}
by_name = {}
for subject in known:
    by_name.setdefault(subject.rsplit('/', 1)[-1], set()).add(subject)


def resolve(subject, exact):
    if exact:
        return subject if subject in known else None
    match = by_name.get(subject.rsplit('/', 1)[-1], set())
    return next(iter(match)) if len(match) == 1 else None


texts = {}
for exact in (True, False):
    for subject, text in raw_texts:
        target = resolve(subject, exact)
        if target is not None:
            texts.setdefault(target, text)
if next_step is not None:
    next_step = resolve(next_step, True) or resolve(next_step, False)

findings, seen, high_given, from_model = [], set(), False, 0


def add(rule, subject, severity, title, default, evidence):
    global high_given, from_model
    if (rule, subject) in seen:
        return
    seen.add((rule, subject))
    if subject == next_step and not high_given:
        severity, high_given = 'HIGH', True
    text = texts.get(subject)
    from_model += text is not None
    findings.append({'ruleKey': rule, 'subject': subject, 'severity': severity, 'title': title,
                     'description': safe(text or default), 'evidence': evidence,
                     'tags': ['backend', 'testing']})


many = len(untested) > 200
for index, (subject, loc) in enumerate(untested):
    add('test-coverage.untested-class', subject, 'LOW' if many and index >= 30 else 'MEDIUM',
        'No test: ' + name(subject),
        'Add a dedicated test for %s; an existing test in the same package serves as a template.' % name(subject),
        '%s LOC' % loc)
for subject, ratio, percent in thin:
    add('test-coverage.thin-test', subject, 'LOW', 'Thin test: ' + name(subject),
        'Add tests for %s: %s @Test per public line.' % (name(subject), ratio),
        '%s @Test/public (%s%%)' % (ratio, percent))

body = '\n'.join(markdown).strip()
print(body)
print()
print('Envelope from the measurement: %d findings (%s untested, %s thin), AI texts for %d, '
      'default text for %d, next step %s.'
      % (len(findings), untested_total if untested_total is not None else 'without header line',
         thin_total if thin_total is not None else 'without header line', from_model, len(findings) - from_model,
         'marked as HIGH' if high_given else 'not found in the measurement, no HIGH'))
print('<!-- mysuricates:audit-result:v1')
print(json.dumps({'snapshotComplete': complete, 'expectedFindings': len(findings), 'findings': findings},
                 ensure_ascii=False))
print('-->')
PY

config.label: Gate-Verdict
config.command:
set -- {{ block.metrics.output }}
METRICS=${1:-}
set -- {{ block.report.output }}
REPORT=${1:-}
# The gate follows the last gate_status line of the report itself, not the short form of the former
# block "Ergebnis erklaeren": its free text ("7,1/10 (YELLOW)") sent the gate into the fallback.
# A line counts only with exactly one verdict word after the colon and at most Markdown (* _ `) and
# whitespace before and after it: the template line "gate_status: GREEN if ..., YELLOW if ...",
# returned unchanged, does not count - otherwise its first word would decide.
VERDICT=$(printf '%s\n' "$REPORT" \
  | grep -iE '^[[:space:]*_>`-]*gate_status[*_`]*:[[:space:]*_`]*(RED|YELLOW|GREEN)[[:space:]*_`]*$' \
  | tail -1 | grep -oiE 'RED|YELLOW|GREEN' | head -1 | tr '[:lower:]' '[:upper:]')

# Check completeness deterministically before the Markdown gate status counts: the Audit
# Center treats a valid envelope as a complete snapshot and sets every finding missing from it
# to RESOLVED. An envelope with snapshotComplete=true and too few findings therefore reports
# untested classes as fixed. And snapshotComplete=false silently records the run as INVALID
# — without this check the gate would still stay green.
# As in the ingestion (AuditResultParser), only the last envelope counts: if the model repeats
# the last report including its envelope, both would count otherwise. As in the parser, an envelope
# starts with "<!--", the marker and the start of the JSON; a quoted marker without JSON does not count.
# Inside an open envelope a new one starts only at the beginning of a line; in the middle of a line it
# is a quote in the text of a finding. It ends with "}" before "-->". If the last one stays open because
# the answer is cut off, it counts as missing instead of as the repeated old one.
ENVELOPE=$(printf '%s\n' "$REPORT" | awk '
  /<!--[ \t\r]*mysuricates:audit-result:v1[ \t\r]*([{]|$)/ && (!inside || /^[ \t\r]*<!--[ \t\r]*mysuricates:audit-result:v1/) {
    buf = ""; last = ""; inside = 1
  }
  inside { buf = buf $0 "\n" }
  inside && /-->/ && buf ~ /[}][ \t\r\n]*-->/ { inside = 0; last = buf }
  END { printf "%s", last }')
EXPECTED=$(printf '%s\n' "$METRICS" | sed -n 's/^EXPECTED FINDINGS: *\([0-9][0-9]*\).*/\1/p' | tail -1)
DELIVERED=$(printf '%s\n' "$ENVELOPE" | grep -o '"ruleKey"' | wc -l | tr -d ' ')

if [ -z "$ENVELOPE" ]; then
  echo 'Coverage coach: envelope missing'
  echo 'gate_status: RED'
  echo 'gate_category: audit-invalid'
  echo 'gate_description: report block delivered no mysuricates:audit-result:v1 envelope — no findings were taken over'
elif printf '%s' "$ENVELOPE" | tr -d ' ' | grep -q '"snapshotComplete":false'; then
  echo 'Coverage coach: snapshot reported as incomplete'
  echo 'gate_status: RED'
  echo 'gate_category: audit-invalid'
  echo 'gate_description: envelope reports snapshotComplete=false — the run is recorded as INVALID, the findings stay at their previous state'
elif [ -z "$EXPECTED" ]; then
  echo 'Coverage coach: target size missing'
  echo 'gate_status: RED'
  echo 'gate_category: audit-incomplete'
  echo 'gate_description: measuring block delivered no line "EXPECTED FINDINGS" — the completeness of the snapshot cannot be checked'
elif [ "$DELIVERED" -ne "$EXPECTED" ]; then
  echo 'Coverage coach: snapshot incomplete'
  echo 'gate_status: RED'
  echo 'gate_category: audit-incomplete'
  echo "gate_description: envelope contains $DELIVERED findings, $EXPECTED were expected — missing classes would wrongly count as fixed (RESOLVED)"
elif [ "$VERDICT" = RED ]; then
  echo 'Coverage coach: CRITICAL'
  echo 'gate_status: RED'
  echo 'gate_category: test-coverage'
  echo 'gate_description: test coverage critical'
elif [ "$VERDICT" = YELLOW ]; then
  echo 'Coverage coach: improvement needed'
  echo 'gate_status: YELLOW'
  echo 'gate_category: test-coverage'
  echo 'gate_description: test coverage can be improved'
elif [ "$VERDICT" = GREEN ]; then
  echo "Coverage coach: OK ($DELIVERED of $EXPECTED findings in the snapshot)"
  echo 'gate_status: GREEN'
  echo 'gate_category: test-coverage'
  echo 'gate_description: test coverage sufficient'
else
  echo 'Coverage coach: INCOMPLETE'
  echo 'gate_status: YELLOW'
  echo 'gate_category: test-coverage'
  echo 'gate_description: result incomplete — no gate_status line in the report (AI block failed or unclear)'
fi
